l: dataset, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RAG Workflow / Query Classification
s: The dataset contains 111K samples covering 15 different types of tasks. It includes 64K samples labeled “retrieval required” and 47K labeled “no retrieval required.”

l: 15 task types, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RAG Workflow / Query Classification
s: The 15 task types categorize queries according to whether they provide sufficient information for answering. Tasks based entirely on user-given information are labeled “sufficient,” while others are labeled “insufficient,” indicating that retrieval may be necessary.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: The unit concerns Chunking documents to improve retrieval precision and avoid length issues in LLMs. It compares token-level, semantic-level, and sentence-level approaches, selecting Sentence-level Chunking for the study because it balances simplicity and semantic preservation. It examines Chunk Size, Chunking Techniques, Metadata Addition, and Embedding Model as four dimensions of chunking. The study selects LLM-Embedder based on the evaluation module of FlagEmbedding for its balance of performance and size, while deferring detailed metadata analysis and related comparisons to future work and Appendix A.2.

l: document chunking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: Chunking divides documents into smaller segments to enhance retrieval precision and avoid length issues in LLMs. It can operate at token, sentence, or semantic levels, and the study examines it through chunk size, chunking techniques, metadata addition, and embedding model.

l: Sentence-level Chunking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: Sentence-level Chunking preserves text semantics while remaining simple and efficient. The study uses it as its selected chunking approach.

l: Chunk Size, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: Chunk Size significantly affects performance. Larger chunks provide more context and may improve comprehension but increase processing time, while smaller chunks improve retrieval recall and reduce time but may lack sufficient context.

l: Chunking Techniques, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: Chunking Techniques include advanced methods such as small-to-big and sliding window approaches. These methods organize relationships among chunk blocks by matching queries with small blocks and returning larger blocks that include the matched blocks and contextual information.

l: Metadata Addition, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: Metadata Addition can include titles, keywords, and hypothetical questions in chunk blocks. It may improve retrieval, enable additional post-processing options, and help LLMs understand retrieved information; detailed study of metadata inclusion is deferred to future work.

l: embedding models, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: The Embedding Model is important for effective semantic matching between queries and chunk blocks. The study selects LLM-Embedder based on the evaluation module of FlagEmbedding because of its balance of performance and size.

l: LLM-Embedder, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: LLM-Embedder is selected by the study as the embedding model for semantic matching between queries and chunk blocks. It is chosen for its balance of performance and size according to the evaluation module of FlagEmbedding.

l: retrieval, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: Retrieval is improved by chunking documents into smaller segments, with the goal of increasing precision and avoiding LLM length issues. Smaller chunks can improve retrieval recall, while metadata and advanced chunking techniques can further improve retrieval quality.

l: study, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Chunking
s: The study uses sentence-level chunking and examines chunk size, chunking techniques, metadata addition, and embedding model. It selects LLM-Embedder for its balance of performance and size, while presenting further discussions and comparative experiments in Appendix A.2.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: The unit concerns vector databases and their evaluation for research use. Vector databases store embedding vectors with metadata and support efficient document retrieval through indexing and approximate nearest neighbor methods. Five open-source vector databases, Weaviate, Faiss, Chroma, Qdrant, and Milvus, were compared using four criteria: multiple index types, billion-scale vector support, hybrid search, and cloud-native capabilities. Milvus was identified as the most comprehensive solution because it met all four criteria and outperformed the other evaluated options.

l: Vector Databases, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: Vector databases store embedding vectors with metadata and enable efficient retrieval of documents relevant to queries through indexing and approximate nearest neighbor methods. They were evaluated for flexibility, scalability, and ease of deployment in modern, cloud-based infrastructures.

l: multiple index types, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: Multiple index types provide flexibility for optimizing searches according to different data characteristics and use cases. They were one of the four criteria used to evaluate vector databases.

l: billion-scale vector support, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: Billion-scale vector support is important for handling large datasets in LLM applications. It was one of the four criteria used to evaluate vector databases.

l: Hybrid, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: Hybrid search combines vector search with traditional keyword search to enhance retrieval accuracy. It was one of the four criteria used to evaluate vector databases.

l: cloud-native capabilities, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: Cloud-native capabilities support seamless integration, scalability, and management in cloud environments. They were one of the four criteria used to evaluate vector databases.

l: Milvus, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: Milvus was identified as the most comprehensive solution among the evaluated databases. It met all four essential criteria and outperformed the other open-source options.

l: open-source vector databases, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Databases
s: The open-source vector databases compared in the evaluation were Weaviate, Faiss, Chroma, Qdrant, and Milvus. They were assessed according to multiple index types, billion-scale vector support, hybrid search, and cloud-native capabilities.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: The retrieval module selects top-k relevant documents from a pre-built corpus, while a generation model uses them to formulate responses. The study evaluates query rewriting, query decomposition, and pseudo-documents generation with LLM-Embedder as the query and document encoder. It compares BM25 sparse retrieval, Contriever dense retrieval, and hybrid search on the TREC DL 2019 and 2020 passage ranking datasets. Hybrid Search with HyDE is recommended for performance, while hybrid search with the original embedding is recommended when efficiency and latency are prioritized.

l: retrieval, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: The retrieval module selects the top-k relevant documents from a pre-built corpus according to similarity between the query and documents. Its performance can be negatively affected when original queries have poor expression or limited semantic information.

l: query transformation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Query transformation is evaluated as a way to improve retrieval by addressing weaknesses in original queries. The evaluated methods are query rewriting, query decomposition, and pseudo-documents generation.

l: query rewriting, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Query rewriting refines queries to better match relevant documents. It is prompted through an LLM in accordance with the Rewrite-Retrieve-Read framework, but it does not improve retrieval performance as effectively as HyDE and hybrid search.

l: query decomposition, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Query decomposition retrieves documents using sub-questions derived from the original query. It is described as more complex to comprehend and handle, and it does not enhance retrieval performance as effectively as HyDE and hybrid search.

l: pseudo-documents generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Pseudo-documents generation creates a hypothetical document from a user query and uses the hypothetical answer's embedding to retrieve similar documents. It is evaluated as a query transformation approach for improving retrieval.

l: HyDE, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: HyDE is identified as a notable implementation of pseudo-documents generation. Combining HyDE with hybrid search produces the highest scores in the reported evaluation.

l: Hybrid, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Hybrid search combines lexical-based and vector search, specifically sparse retrieval with dense retrieval. Hybrid Search with HyDE achieves the highest scores, while hybrid search using the original embedding offers notable performance with relatively low latency and is recommended when efficiency is prioritized.

l: BM25, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: BM25 is used for sparse retrieval and serves as one of the two robust unsupervised retrieval baselines. It is also used as the sparse component of hybrid search.

l: Contriever, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Contriever is used for dense retrieval as an unsupervised contrastive encoder. It serves as the second robust unsupervised retrieval baseline in the evaluation.

l: LLM-Embedder, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: LLM-Embedder, recommended in Section 3.2, is used as the query and document encoder for evaluating the query transformation methods. Supervised methods outperform unsupervised methods, and LLM-Embedder achieves the highest scores when combined with HyDE and hybrid search.

l: TREC DL 2019 passage ranking dataset, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: The TREC DL 2019 passage ranking dataset is used to evaluate different search methods.

l: sparse retrieval, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Sparse retrieval is represented by BM25 in the study. It forms one component of hybrid search.

l: dense retrieval, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Retrieval Methods
s: Dense retrieval is represented by Contriever in the study and uses vector-based representations. It forms the other component of hybrid search.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: Reranking Methods improve retrieval by reordering documents so that the most relevant information appears first. The unit compares DLM Reranking, which uses classification with deep language models, and TILDE Reranking, which uses query-term likelihoods for greater efficiency. Experiments on the MS MARCO Passage ranking dataset used monoT5, monoBERT, RankLLaMA, and TILDEv2. The text recommends monoT5 as a balance of performance and efficiency, RankLLaMA for best performance, and TILDEv2 for the fastest experience on a fixed collection.

l: Reranking Methods, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: Reranking Methods enhance the relevance of retrieved documents by reordering them so that the most pertinent information appears at the top. The unit considers DLM Reranking and TILDE Reranking.

l: Reranking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: Reranking is applied after initial retrieval to improve the similarity between the query and the top-ranked documents.

l: DLM Reranking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: DLM Reranking uses classification with deep language models and generally provides the best performance with reduced efficiency. It ranks documents according to the probability assigned to the “true” token for each query.

l: TILDE Reranking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: TILDE Reranking focuses on query likelihoods and is designed for efficiency. It rapidly reranks candidate documents by summing pre-calculated log probabilities for the query tokens.

l: deep language models, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: Deep language models are fine-tuned to predict “true” or “false” from a user query and candidate document concatenated as input. DLM rerankers use the probability of the “true” token to rank documents.

l: query likelihoods, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: Query likelihoods are used by TILDE Reranking to estimate the probabilities of individual query terms. Conventional query likelihood models calculate conditional probabilities based on preceding query tokens, while TILDE considers each query term independently.

l: user query, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: The user query is concatenated with a candidate document as input when DLM models are fine-tuned for relevance classification.

l: candidate documents, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: Candidate documents are ranked by DLM models according to the probability of the “true” token. For TILDE, candidate documents are preprocessed at indexing so they can be rapidly reranked using pre-calculated log probabilities.

l: TILDE, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: TILDE independently considers each query term and predicts token probabilities across the entire vocabulary. It enables rapid reranking by summing the pre-calculated log probabilities corresponding to query tokens for each document.

l: TILDEv2, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: TILDEv2 improves efficiency and reduces index size by indexing only document-present tokens, using NCE loss, and applying document expansion. It is described as ideal for the quickest experience on a fixed collection.

l: monoT5, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: monoT5 was used in the experiments and is recommended as a comprehensive method that balances performance and efficiency.

l: RankLLaMA, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: RankLLaMA was used in the experiments and is considered suitable for achieving the best performance.

l: MS MARCO Passage ranking dataset, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: The experiments were conducted on the MS MARCO Passage ranking dataset.

l: MS MARCO experiments, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reranking Methods
s: The MS MARCO experiments used implementations from PyGaggle and TILDE, with modifications, and evaluated monoT5, monoBERT, RankLLaMA, and TILDEv2. The reranking results are reported in Table 10.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: Document Repacking concerns how the order of documents affects subsequent processes such as LLM response generation. It introduces a compact repacking module used after reranking, with three methods: forward, reverse, and sides. Forward orders documents by descending reranking relevance scores, while reverse orders them ascending. Inspired by Liu et al. (2024a), the sides method places relevant information at the head or tail and is selected as the default method after testing.

l: Document Repacking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: Document Repacking addresses the effect of document order on subsequent processes such as LLM response generation. It uses a compact repacking module after reranking and selects sides as the default method.

l: documents, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: Documents are reordered after reranking according to the selected repacking method. They can be arranged by descending relevance, ascending relevance, or with relevant information placed at the head or tail.

l: compact repacking module, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: The compact repacking module is incorporated into the workflow after reranking. It provides the forward, reverse, and sides repacking methods.

l: Reranking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: Reranking supplies the relevancy scores used to order documents during repacking. The repacking module operates after reranking.

l: forward, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: Forward repacks documents in descending order of their relevancy scores from the reranking phase.

l: reverse, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: Reverse repacks documents in ascending order of their relevancy scores from the reranking phase.

l: sides, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Repacking
s: Sides is inspired by Liu et al. (2024a), which concluded that performance is optimal when relevant information is placed at the head or tail of the input. It is selected as the default repacking method after being tested with other modules.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: This unit concerns summarization methods for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), where redundant information and long prompts can reduce response accuracy and slow inference. It distinguishes extractive methods, which select important sentences, from abstractive methods, which synthesize information across documents, and focuses on query-based methods. Recomp and LongLLMLingua are evaluated on NQ, TriviaQA, and HotpotQA; Recomp is recommended for its strong performance, while LongLLMLingua is considered an alternative because of its better generalization capabilities.

l: Summarization, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: Summarization reduces redundant or unnecessary information in retrieved documents and can make prompts shorter. It may be extractive, selecting important sentences, or abstractive, synthesizing information from multiple documents.

l: RAG, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: Retrieval-augmented generation can provide redundant information and lengthy prompts, creating challenges for accurate responses and efficient inference. Query-based summarization methods are used to compress retrieved information within its pipeline.

l: large language models, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: Long prompts can slow the inference process of large language models and may prevent them from generating accurate responses.

l: query-based summarization, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: Query-based summarization focuses on information relevant to a query. The unit evaluates query-based methods because retrieval-augmented generation retrieves information relevant to queries.

l: Recomp, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: Recomp has extractive and abstractive compressors: the extractive compressor selects useful sentences, while the abstractive compressor synthesizes information from multiple documents. It shows outstanding performance on NQ, TriviaQA, and HotpotQA, and is recommended.

l: LongLLMLingua, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: LongLLMLingua improves LLMLingua by focusing on key information related to the query. It does not perform well on the evaluated datasets but demonstrates better generalization capabilities because it was not trained on them, so it is considered an alternative method.

l: NQ, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: NQ is one of the three benchmark datasets used to evaluate Recomp and LongLLMLingua.

l: TriviaQA, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: TriviaQA is one of the three benchmark datasets used to evaluate Recomp and LongLLMLingua.

l: HotpotQA, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Summarization
s: HotpotQA is one of the three benchmark datasets used to evaluate Recomp and LongLLMLingua.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: This unit examines fine-tuning the generator in a RAG system while leaving retriever fine-tuning for future work. It compares training with relevant documents, randomly retrieved documents, mixtures of both, and duplicated relevant documents, using Llama-2-7B as the base model. The study evaluates ground-truth coverage on QA and reading comprehension datasets and finds that Mgr, trained with mixed relevant and random contexts, performs best with gold or mixed contexts. The results suggest that including a few relevant and randomly selected documents during training improves robustness to irrelevant information while preserving effective use of relevant contexts.

l: Generator Fine-tuning, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Generator Fine-tuning investigates how relevant and irrelevant contexts affect generator performance while retriever fine-tuning is left for future exploration. It trains models with different compositions of relevant, random, mixed, and duplicated contexts.

l: generator, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: The generator is fine-tuned using the negative log-likelihood of the ground-truth output. Its performance is evaluated with different retrieved-context configurations and without retrieval.

l: RAG system, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: The RAG system receives a query and contexts as input. The unit studies how fine-tuning the generator affects its use of relevant and irrelevant contexts.

l: contexts, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Contexts are denoted by D and are varied during training and evaluation. They may contain a relevant document, a random document, both, two copies of a relevant document, or no retrieved context.

l: relevant document (query), Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: The relevant document is denoted as dgold and is relevant to the query. It is used alone, together with a randomly selected document, or duplicated in training and evaluation configurations.

l: randomly retrieved document, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: The randomly retrieved document is denoted as drandom and is sampled randomly. It is used alone or mixed with a query-relevant document to assess the generator's robustness to irrelevant information.

l: Dgr, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Dgr is an augmented context containing one relevant document and one randomly selected document. The model trained with this context, Mgr, performs best when evaluated with gold or mixed contexts.

l: base LM generator, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: The base LM generator is denoted as Mb and is not fine-tuned. It is distinguished from the models fine-tuned under the different context configurations.

l: Mgr, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Mgr is the model fine-tuned with a mixture of relevant and random documents. It performs best when provided with either gold or mixed contexts, suggesting improved robustness to irrelevant information and effective use of relevant contexts.

l: QA datasets, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: QA datasets are among the datasets used to fine-tune and evaluate the models. Their relatively short answers motivate the use of ground-truth coverage as the evaluation metric.

l: reading comprehension datasets, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Reading comprehension datasets are also used to fine-tune and evaluate the models. Evaluation is conducted on their validation sets with multiple context configurations.

l: ground-truth coverage, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Ground-truth coverage is used as the evaluation metric because QA task answers are relatively short. It measures performance based on whether the gold response appears in the model's output.

l: Exact Match, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Exact Match is applied in a more lenient form. The score is based on the presence of the gold response in the model's output.

l: Llama-2-7B, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Llama-2-7B is selected as the base model for the generator fine-tuning experiments.

l: relevant and random documents during training, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Generator Fine-tuning
s: Training with a few relevant and randomly selected documents is identified as the best approach. This mixture improves robustness to irrelevant information while maintaining effective utilization of relevant contexts.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: The section investigates best RAG practices by sequentially optimizing individual modules and selecting the most effective alternatives. It uses Llama2-7B-Chat as the generator, with each query augmented by a few randomly selected and relevant documents. Milvus builds a vector database containing 10 million English Wikipedia texts and 4 million medical data texts. The study also examines the impact of removing the Query Classification, Reranking, and Summarization modules.

l: RAG, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: RAG is investigated to identify optimal implementation practices across its modules.

l: best RAG practices, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: Best RAG practices are studied through an iterative process that sequentially optimizes modules and selects the most effective option among alternatives.

s: The modules are optimized sequentially, beginning with default practices and continuing through the final summarization module.

l: Llama2-7B-Chat, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: Llama2-7B-Chat is used as the model fine-tuned for generation.

l: generator, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: The generator uses Llama2-7B-Chat, with each query augmented by a few randomly selected and relevant documents.

l: Milvus, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: Milvus is used to build the vector database.

l: English Wikipedia, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: English Wikipedia contributes 10 million texts to the vector database.

l: medical data, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best RAG Practices
s: Medical data contributes 4 million texts to the vector database.

s: The impact of removing Query Classification is investigated to assess its contribution.

s: The impact of removing Reranking is investigated to assess its contribution.

l: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The Comprehensive Evaluation assesses RAG systems across Commonsense Reasoning, Fact Checking, Open-Domain QA, MultiHop QA, and Medical QA using task-specific metrics and five RAG capabilities. Results show that query classification improves the average score and reduces latency by avoiding unnecessary retrieval, while hybrid retrieval, reranking, reverse repacking, and Recomp summarization improve response quality. Hybrid with HyDE achieves the highest reported RAG score of 0.58 but requires 11.71 seconds per query, whereas monoT5 is the strongest tested reranker. Recomp generally outperforms LongLLMLingua because it preserves source-content integrity, although removing summarization can reduce latency.

l: RAG system, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The RAG system was evaluated across five NLP task categories using a common corpus and up to 500 subsampled examples per dataset. Its performance improved through query classification, hybrid retrieval, reranking, reverse repacking, and summarization.

l: Comprehensive Evaluation, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The Comprehensive Evaluation measured RAG capabilities on Commonsense Reasoning, Fact Checking, Open-Domain QA, MultiHop QA, and Medical QA. It used accuracy for Commonsense Reasoning, Fact Checking, and Medical QA, and token-level F1 and Exact Match for the two QA tasks.

l: Commonsense Reasoning, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: Commonsense Reasoning was one of the evaluated NLP tasks, with accuracy used as its task metric.

l: Fact Checking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: Fact Checking was one of the evaluated NLP tasks, with accuracy used as its task metric.

l: Open-Domain QA, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: Open-Domain QA was evaluated using token-level F1 score and Exact Match score. The two QA tasks were scored simultaneously using GPT.

l: MultiHop QA, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: MultiHop QA was evaluated using token-level F1 score and Exact Match score. The two QA tasks were scored simultaneously using GPT.

l: Medical QA, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: Medical QA was one of the evaluated NLP tasks, with accuracy used as its task metric.

l: RAG score, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The RAG score was calculated by averaging Faithfulness, Context Relevancy, Answer Relevancy, Answer Correctness, and Retrieval Similarity. Hybrid with HyDE achieved the highest reported RAG score of 0.58, while the selected full configuration reported an overall average of 0.443 in the table.

l: Query Classification, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The query classification module distinguishes queries that require retrieval from those containing complete information. It increased the average overall score from 0.428 to 0.443 and reduced latency from 16.41 to 11.58 seconds per query.

l: retrieval, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The retrieval module performed best when dense retrieval was combined with BM25, because semantic matching and exact term matching compensate for each other's weaknesses. Hybrid with HyDE achieved the highest RAG score but incurred greater computational cost, while Hybrid or Original were recommended when lower latency is needed.

l: Reranking, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The reranking module was important for maintaining high-quality results, as performance dropped without reranking. Among the tested DLM-based rerankers, monoT5 outperformed monoBERT and RankLLaMA.

l: compact repacking module, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis
s: The repacking module performed best with the Reverse configuration, which achieved an RAG score of 0.560. This indicates that placing more relevant context closer to the query improves results.

l: Summarization, Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Comprehensive Evaluation .. Results and Analysis

s: The experiments evaluate SELF-RAG and diverse baselines on closed-set, short-form generation, and long-form generation tasks using metrics for correctness, factuality, fluency, and citation quality. The datasets include PubHealth, ARC-Challenge, PopQA, TriviaQA-unfiltered, a biography generation task, and ALCE-ASQA. l: SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: This unit evaluates SELF-RAG against supervised, proprietary, and retrieval-augmented baselines across tasks including PubHealth, PopQA, and ASQA. SELF-RAG generally outperforms non-proprietary models and improves citation precision and recall, while sometimes surpassing ChatGPT. Ablations show that retrieval, critic training, adaptive retrieval, and ISSUP-guided search each contribute to performance. Further analyses examine inference-time customization, retrieval frequency, training-data scale, and the reliability of reflection tokens.

l: SELF-RAG, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: SELF-RAG substantially outperforms supervised fine-tuned language models without retrieval and achieves the best performance among non-proprietary language-model-based systems across the evaluated tasks. It learns to retrieve, generate, and critique passages and its own generations using reflection tokens, and its performance benefits from training scale, adaptive retrieval, and ISSUP-guided beam search.

l: retrieval-augmented generation, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: Conventional retrieval-augmented generation systems often struggle on tasks requiring more than copying or extracting substrings from retrieved passages. SELF-RAG outperforms existing retrieval-augmented approaches on many tasks by selecting and evaluating retrieved information rather than using top passages naively.

l: large language models, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: The evaluated large language models include supervised fine-tuned models, instruction-tuned models, proprietary models, and retrieval-augmented systems. SELF-RAG improves over larger or otherwise strong language models on several tasks, although smaller SELF-RAG models can sometimes achieve higher factual precision because they generate shorter, more grounded outputs.

l: baselines, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: Baselines without retrieval generally trail SELF-RAG, while retrieval-equipped baselines show substantial gains on PopQA and biography generation but limited gains on PubHealth and ARC-Challenge. Most baselines with retrieval also struggle to improve citation accuracy.

l: PubHealth, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: On PubHealth, SELF-RAG outperforms the evaluated baselines, while many retrieval-equipped baselines do not improve notably over their non-retrieval counterparts. Performance deteriorates less when SELF-RAG retrieves less frequently than it does on PopQA.

l: PopQA, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: SELF-RAG achieves strong performance on PopQA and benefits substantially from increased training-data size. Always retrieving the top passage causes a large performance drop compared with adaptive retrieval.

l: ALCE-ASQA, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: On ASQA, SELF-RAG shows substantially higher citation precision and recall than all models except ChatGPT and surpasses ChatGPT in citation precision. Its performance is harmed when the top retrieved passage is always used or when ISSUP is removed during critique-guided beam search.

l: ChatGPT, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: ChatGPT outperforms smaller language models on ASQA according to the cited findings, but SELF-RAG narrows this gap. SELF-RAG also surpasses ChatGPT in ASQA citation precision.

l: citation precision, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: Increasing the inference-time weight assigned to ISSUP improves citation precision by emphasizing whether generations are supported by evidence. SELF-RAG has higher citation precision than the evaluated models on ASQA except for ChatGPT, and it surpasses ChatGPT on this metric.

l: reflection tokens, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: Reflection tokens enable SELF-RAG to decide when to retrieve and to critique relevance and support for passages and generations. Human annotators found that the predicted ISREL and ISSUP tokens were mostly aligned with their assessments.

l: ISSUP reflection token, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: ISSUP measures how well an output is supported by a text passage and can be assigned greater weight during inference. Increasing its weight improves citation precision but lowers MAUVE, while removing ISSUP from critique-guided beam search hurts ASQA performance.

l: adaptive retrieval with threshold, SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection, RESULTS AND ANALYSIS / 5.1 / MAIN RESULTS .. 5.2 / ANALYSIS
s: Adaptive retrieval uses the predicted probability of retrieval-related reward tokens and a threshold to control retrieval frequency. Increasing the threshold reduces retrieval, with smaller performance deterioration on PubHealth than on PopQA.

s: Using retrieved passages indiscriminately is less effective than SELF-RAG's fine-grained selection and critique of passages. Always using the top passage causes large drops on PopQA and ASQA, demonstrating that passage relevance alone is insufficient.

s: SELF-RAG evaluates whether generated claims are supported by cited evidence and can prioritize this criterion during generation. Human evaluations found that its answers were often plausible and supported by relevant passages, particularly on short-form PopQA.
